lines: My uncle kept a rooster named Pastor, who woke the whole compound at four every morning, regardless of the weather, the hour, or our feelings on the matter.
I hated him with the pure, uncomplicated hatred of a teenager denied sleep.
Years later, in a season when nothing was working, a friend asked me what I was waiting for before I began again.
I said I was waiting for it to be light.
The rooster does not wait for the sun.
He crows into the dark, with no evidence whatsoever, because he knows something the dark has not been told: that morning is already on its way.
I have begun to think faith is mostly that.
Not even hope in the large and shining sense.
Just a stubborn, ordinary voice, lifted at four a.m., declaring to the unlit yard that this, too, will turn.
I still do not forgive him for the sleep.
But I have forgiven him for everything else.
